title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Explore the essential streets and corridors of Morningside Heights that define the off-campus experience for Barnard students.

cards.title: The Main Academic Artery
cards.subtitle: Broadway between 116th and 120th Streets
cards.notes: Walk this primary corridor to transition between Barnard's gates and Columbia's main campus while passing the 116th St subway station.
cards.short_summary: The central commercial and transit spine connecting Barnard College to the rest of the Columbia University campus and Manhattan.
cards.evidence_claim: Barnard College is located on the Upper West Side of Manhattan between 116th and 120th Streets along the west side of Broadway.
cards.access_notes: Public city street accessible 24/7; contains the 116th St-Columbia University subway entrance.

cards.title: The Cultural Corridor
cards.subtitle: Amsterdam Avenue near 112th Street
cards.notes: Visit this block to find the Hungarian Pastry Shop and the Cathedral of St. John the Divine, popular for off-campus study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A major avenue east of campus known for its historic architecture, cafes, and proximity to the world's largest cathedral.
cards.evidence_claim: Amsterdam Avenue is lined with monumental sights like the Cathedral of St. John the Divine and student favorites like The Hungarian Pastry Shop.
cards.source_title: A Day in Morningside Heights | Barnard College
cards.access_notes: Public avenue; businesses like Hungarian Pastry Shop have individual operating hours.

cards.title: The Southern Gateway
cards.subtitle: West 110th Street (Cathedral Parkway)
cards.notes: Head to this block for essential services like Westside Market and access to the northwest corner of Central Park.
cards.short_summary: A major cross-town street serving as the southern boundary of Morningside Heights and a hub for student groceries and park access.
cards.evidence_claim: Westside Market is located on the corner of 110th Street and Broadway, serving as an essential stop for neighborhood shopping.
cards.source_title: Your guide to navigating Morningside Heights - Columbia Spectator
cards.access_notes: Public street; Westside Market is typically open 24 hours.

cards.title: The Literary Block
cards.subtitle: West 112th Street between Broadway and Amsterdam
cards.notes: Browse the shelves at Book Culture on this block, a primary source for course texts and community literary events.
cards.short_summary: A quiet residential and commercial block home to independent bookstores and student-frequented cafes.
cards.evidence_claim: Book Culture has a location on 112th Street near Columbia that offers a wide selection of books and textbooks.
cards.source_title: Your guide to navigating Morningside Heights - Columbia Spectator
cards.access_notes: Public street; Book Culture typically opens daily at 10:00 AM.

cards.title: The Residential Hub
cards.subtitle: West 114th Street near Broadway
cards.notes: Walk past historic brownstones and Columbia residence halls on this street, which borders the iconic Butler Library.
cards.short_summary: A street dominated by university housing and Greek life brownstones, providing a classic collegiate atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: West 114th Street is a major street for campus housing, featuring six Columbia residence halls and eleven brownstones.
cards.access_notes: Public street; residential buildings require CUID for entry.

cards.title: The Pedestrian Plaza
cards.subtitle: West 116th Street (College Walk)
cards.notes: Cross Broadway to enter College Walk, a pedestrian-only stretch that serves as the heart of the Morningside campus.
cards.short_summary: A former city street transformed into a central pedestrian thoroughfare connecting the east and west sides of the university.
cards.evidence_claim: The block of 116th Street between Broadway and Amsterdam Avenue was permanently closed to vehicular traffic in 1953 and turned into College Walk.
cards.access_notes: Open to pedestrians 24/7; connects the main campus gates at Broadway.

cards.title: The Scenic Promenade
cards.subtitle: Riverside Drive at 122nd Street
cards.notes: Stroll along this drive to reach Sakura Park, famous for its cherry blossoms and views of the Hudson River.
cards.short_summary: A picturesque residential drive bordering Riverside Park, offering a quiet escape from the urban grid.
cards.evidence_claim: Sakura Park along Riverside Drive is lined with cherry blossom trees, perfect for a walk.
cards.source_title: A Day in Morningside Heights | Barnard College
cards.access_notes: Public drive and park; park is open from 6:00 AM to 1:00 AM.

cards.title: The Northern Boundary
cards.subtitle: West 120th Street between Broadway and Amsterdam
cards.notes: Find Teachers College and the northern edge of the main campus on this street, which marks the transition to Manhattanville.
cards.short_summary: A key academic street housing Teachers College and providing a link to the university's northern expansion.
cards.evidence_claim: Teachers College campus is located on Broadway and occupies two blocks between West 120th St. and West 122nd St.
cards.source_title: Morningside Heights | Visit | About - Teachers College
cards.access_notes: Public street; academic buildings have specific security protocols.

cards.title: The Quiet Enclave
cards.subtitle: Claremont Avenue near 120th Street
cards.notes: Explore this residential avenue west of Broadway, home to many Barnard and Columbia faculty and graduate students.
cards.short_summary: A serene, tree-lined street known for its pre-war apartment buildings and proximity to Riverside Church.
cards.evidence_claim: Claremont Avenue is a residential street in Morningside Heights home to institutions like the Manhattan School of Music and university housing.
cards.access_notes: Public residential street; quiet hours are generally respected.

cards.title: The Harlem Connection
cards.subtitle: West 125th Street at Broadway
cards.notes: Walk north to this historic Harlem thoroughfare to visit the Manhattanville campus and the Jerome L. Greene Science Center.
cards.short_summary: A major cultural and commercial street in Harlem that serves as the anchor for Columbia's new Manhattanville campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Manhattanville campus is located just north of 125th Street, a historic district seeing immense growth.
cards.source_title: About the Manhattanville Campus | Columbia University
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; Manhattanville campus plazas are open to the public.
